sentences.zh: 庞培接管了他认为具有宪政合法性的角色。

sentences.en: Pompey has taken command of what he sees as the kind of the constitutional legitimate, uh, role.
sentences.zh: 他站在绝大多数元老院成员的前面。

sentences.en: Um, he stands at the head of, of the vast majority of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他们逃离了罗马。

sentences.en: They have fled Rome.
sentences.zh: 他们穿过了亚得里亚海。

sentences.en: They've crossed the, um, the Adriatic.
sentences.zh: 他们来到了希腊。

sentences.en: They've come, gone to Greece.
sentences.zh: 恺撒已经控制了西班牙。

sentences.en: Caesar has made sure of Spain.
sentences.zh: 他已经控制了意大利。

sentences.en: He's made sure of Italy.
sentences.zh: 随后他率舰队渡海前往希腊。

sentences.en: He then crosses with his fleet to Greece.
sentences.zh: 他的兵力处于绝对劣势。

sentences.en: He's vastly outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 他最终在法萨卢斯这个地方与庞培的军队遭遇，并在不被看好的情况下击败了庞培。

sentences.en: He ends up meeting with Pompey's armies, um, at a place called Pharsalus and against the odds, he beats Pompey.
sentences.zh: 他为什么能击败庞培？

sentences.en: Why does he beat Pompey?
sentences.zh: 简短告诉我。

sentences.en: Tell me just very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他是一名更优秀的统帅。

sentences.en: He's a better general.
sentences.zh: 他是一个更聪明、更狡猾的统帅。

sentences.en: He's, he's, he's, he's a cleverer, subtler general.
sentences.zh: 庞培过于自信了。

sentences.en: Uh, Pompey is overconfident.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且恺撒率领的是追随了他多年、多年的人。

sentences.en: Um, and Caesar is at the head of men who have been following him for years and years.
sentences.zh: 他们对恺撒有着绝对的信心。

sentences.en: You've had absolute confidence in him.
sentences.zh: 他们的士气高昂至极，坚信自己无所不能。

sentences.en: Whose morale is sky high, who believe that they can do anything.
sentences.zh: 而庞培则很大程度上在躺在功劳簿上吃老本。

sentences.en: Uh, Pompey is very much kind of resting on his laurels.
sentences.zh: 他靠的是声望，但到这个时候，那已经是十多年前的事了，而且他手头并没有足够的军团。

sentences.en: He's drawing on a reputation, but that by this point is a decade and more old and he doesn't have the legions to hand.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，在卢比肯河事件发生前夕，有人向他指出了这一点，而庞培曾说过，

sentences.en: So he had, you know, this had been pointed out to him in the buildup to the Rubicon and Pompey had said,
sentences.zh: 好吧，我只要跺一跺脚，意大利的土地上就会涌现出无数军团。

sentences.en: well, I just have to stamp my foot and legions will emerge from, from out of the soil of Italy.
sentences.zh: 但事情并没有那样发展。

sentences.en: But it didn't work like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，恺撒的军团实在是太精锐了。

sentences.en: You know, Caesar's legions are just too proficient.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，凯撒的军团实在是太熟练了。

sentences.en: Caesar is too, you know, they're too battle honed.
sentences.zh: 凯撒也一样，你知道的，他们的战斗经验太丰富了。

sentences.en: And so Pompey loses, he is, he flees the battlefield and he then has to decide, well, what am I going to do?
sentences.zh: 于是庞培战败了，他逃离了战场，接着他必须决定：好吧，我接下来该怎么办？

sentences.en: And because he, he is the great conqueror of the East, he is the man who had brought much of the near East under Roman power, who has Kings across the near East as his clients.
sentences.zh: 因为他是东方的伟大征服者，正是他将近东的大部分土地置于罗马的统治之下，并在整个近东拥有无数将国王奉为门客的威望。

sentences.en: He assumes that he can draw on them.
sentences.zh: 他以为自己可以向他们寻求支援。

sentences.en: And so he thinks, well, who is the most, who is the richest, who is the most useful of these Royal clients?
sentences.zh: 于是他想，好吧，谁才是这些王室门客中最……最富有、最有用的人呢？

sentences.en: It's the King of Egypt.
sentences.zh: 是埃及国王。

sentences.en: So he decides he will go to Egypt.
sentences.zh: 所以他决定去埃及。

sentences.en: He will go to Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 他要去亚历山大。

sentences.en: He will throw his weight around.
sentences.zh: 他要去摆谱施压。

sentences.en: He will pull rank and he will get enough money to raise money to, to raise troops to go and have another crack at Caesar.
sentences.zh: 他要耍大牌，筹集到足够的资金来招募军队，好再去跟凯撒较量一番。

sentences.en: So that's not, that's not a bad strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以这其实……这其实是个不错的策略。

sentences.en: When you think about it, is it?
sentences.zh: 仔细想想，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's lost Pharsalus, but he knows that the Egyptians owe him because he'd always been very close to
sentences.zh: 他在法萨卢斯战败了，但他知道埃及人欠他人情，因为他一向与……

sentences.en: Auletes, Cleopatra's father.
sentences.zh: 奥勒次（克利奥帕特拉的父亲）关系非常密切。

sentences.en: He knows that Egypt is torn apart by this incipient civil war.
sentences.zh: 他知道埃及正因这场一触即发的内战而分裂。

sentences.en: So he can kind of go in as the strong man.
sentences.zh: 所以他觉得自己可以作为强势人物介入。

sentences.en: And basically he, he knows there's a boy King.
sentences.zh: 而且基本上他知道那里有个年幼的国王。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Pompey just kind of thinks, well, this is, this is great.
sentences.zh: 所以庞培就觉得，这……这太棒了。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, he is the strong man.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他自认为是强势人物。

sentences.en: He sees himself as a strong man and never crosses his mind.
sentences.zh: 他把自己看作强者，从没想过另一种可能。

sentences.en: But the fact that he's lost means that suddenly his image is no longer that of a strong man, but of an absolute loser.
sentences.zh: 但战败的事实意味着，他的形象已不再是一个强者，而是一个彻头彻尾的失败者。

sentences.en: So there's this famous scene, isn't there, where, um, so Ptolemy the 13th, the boy King, Cleopatra is still out there in the sort of the edge of the, beyond Pellysium.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个著名的场景，不是吗？当时，呃，托勒密十三世是个少年国王，而克利奥帕特拉还在佩鲁修姆边缘之外的某个地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, the boy King's ministers, they have this meeting and they say, what are we going to do?
sentences.zh: 呃，少年国王的大臣们召开了一场会议，他们说，我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: Pompey's coming.
sentences.zh: 庞培要来了。

sentences.en: And supposedly there's a guy who's his tutor, Theodotus of Chios, I think it is, Tom, um, who I describe it in my book as a, as an oily man.
sentences.zh: 据说有个家伙是他的老师，好像叫希俄斯的狄奥多图斯吧，汤姆，呃，我在书里把他形容为一个油腔滑调的人。

sentences.en: Not dealing in stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 我可不是在刻意套用刻板印象。

sentences.en: No, well, he behaves in a, I don't know anything about Chios.
sentences.zh: 不，好吧，他的行为举止……我对希俄斯一无所知。

sentences.en: I mean, they may be very unoily for all I know, but, uh, he behaves in a very oily way because he basically says, well,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，据我所知，他们可能一点也不油滑，但是，呃，他的行为极其油滑，因为他基本上是在说……

sentences.en: you know, if we accept Pompey, we make ourselves Julius Caesar's enemies and Pompey will just boss us around and be a pain.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果我们接纳庞培，就会树凯撒这个敌，而且庞培会对我们指手画脚、惹人生厌。

sentences.en: If we turn him away, he will be our enemy.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把他赶走，他就会成为我们的敌人。

sentences.en: And if he then wins, we're in a mess.
sentences.zh: 如果他最后赢了，我们就彻底完蛋了。

sentences.en: And he says, and the quote is, uh, there's only one way to please Caesar and have nothing to fear from Pompey.
sentences.zh: 他说，原话是这样的，呃：“只有一个办法既能取悦凯撒，又不用怕庞培。”

sentences.en: And he says, and that is welcome Pompey and kill him.
sentences.zh: 他说：“那就是欢迎庞培，然后杀了他。”

sentences.en: For as we all know, dead men don't bite, which is such a fantastic, um, such a fantastic line.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，“死人是不会咬人的”，这真是一句绝妙的、呃，绝妙台词。

sentences.en: And then there's this incredible scene, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 然后还有这样一个令人难以置信的场景，不是吗？

sentences.en: Where Pompey, who is, as you say, this ancient war hero, he pitches up on his boat.
sentences.zh: 庞培，正如你所说，这位古代的战争英雄，乘着他的船抵达了。

sentences.en: They send a little fishing boat to greet him.
sentences.zh: 他们派了一艘小渔船去迎接他。

sentences.en: The fishing boat has, um, a kill ass on who is
sentences.zh: 渔船上有，呃，阿基拉斯，他是……

sentences.en: Ptolemy's commander.
sentences.zh: 托勒密的指挥官。

sentences.en: Um, and an old, old associate of Pompey's called Lucius Septimius, who sort of says, um, well, he doesn't say anything at firSt. And Pompey says to him, don't I recognize you?
sentences.zh: 呃，还有一个庞培的老熟人叫卢修斯·塞普蒂米乌斯，他有点像……呃，他起初什么也没说。庞培对他说：“我不认识你吗？”

sentences.en: Didn't use to be an old comrade of mine.
sentences.zh: “你以前不是我的老战友吗？”

sentences.en: Septimius says, yes.
sentences.zh: 塞普蒂米乌斯说：“是的。”

sentences.en: And they, they, they sail back towards the coaSt. And Pompey's got his speech with him that he's going to read to, um, to Ptolemy the 13th, this sort of speech of welcome.
sentences.zh: 然后他们朝岸边驶去。庞培随身带着他准备念给……托勒密十三世听的演讲稿，那是一种欢迎辞。

sentences.en: And it's while he's reading it, I think that they, they begin to pull their knives out of the, out of the scabbards.
sentences.zh: 正当他在朗读的时候，我想，他们开始把匕首从鞘里拔出来了。

sentences.en: And then just as they're approaching the shore, as he can see the boy King on the beach, surrounded by the, the oily tutor, the fleshy eunuch and all
sentences.zh: 就在他们快要靠近岸边时，当他能看到沙滩上的少年国王时，周围簇拥着油滑的导师、肥胖的阉宦和所有……

sentences.en: these other stereotypes, all these other characters, they cut Pompey's head off.
sentences.zh: 这些其他的刻板形象、所有这些角色，他们砍下了庞培的头。

sentences.en: What a twiSt.
sentences.zh: 真是个大反转。

sentences.en: What a twiSt. Do you think that's, do you think Pompey was hard done by there, Tom?
sentences.zh: 真是个大反转。汤姆，你觉得庞培在那里是不是太冤了？

sentences.en: I think he had it coming.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他罪有应得。

sentences.en: You think he had it coming?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他罪有应得？

sentences.en: Well, I'll tell you who else thought,
sentences.zh: 好吧，我告诉你还有谁觉得……

sentences.en: I'll tell you who else thought he had it coming, um, were the Jews because Pompey had, uh, captured
sentences.zh: 我告诉你还有谁觉得他罪有应得，呃，是犹太人，因为庞培曾经攻陷过……

sentences.en: Jerusalem and the temple.
sentences.zh: 耶路撒冷和圣殿。

sentences.en: And of course, no non-Jew was allowed to go into the temple, but Pompey went in and he went right into the Holy of Holies.
sentences.zh: 当然，任何非犹太人都不准进入圣殿，但庞培进去了，他直接走进了至圣所。

sentences.en: And the Jews said that from that point on, everything started going wrong for him.
sentences.zh: 犹太人说，从那时起，他的一切都开始走下坡路了。

sentences.en: Uh, and when the news, um, came out that he'd been, uh, he'd been beheaded.
sentences.zh: 呃，当消息传出他被……他被斩首时。

sentences.en: Um, Jewish poets hailed this as, um, the victory of God over the pride of the dragon instead of Pompey that he had failed to recognize that God alone is great.
sentences.zh: 呃，犹太诗人称颂这为，呃，上帝对恶龙傲慢的胜利，而不是庞培的胜利，因为他没有认出唯有上帝才是伟大的。

sentences.en: Well, so you can see how, how this, this stuff reverberates, you know, and is interpreted in all kinds of different ways by different peoples.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以看到这些事情是如何产生回响的，你知道的，并在不同的人群中被以各种方式解读。

sentences.en: Um, you know, this is huge, huge stuff.
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道的，这是非常、非常重大的人物和事件。

sentences.en: Uh, and of course the, the, the people with whom it reverberates most of all are the Romans.
sentences.zh: 呃，当然，感触最深的还是罗马人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And specifically Julius Caesar, who's come with a very, very light force.
sentences.zh: 尤其是尤利乌斯·凯撒，他带着一支非常、非常轻装的部队赶来。

sentences.en: So not a large number of men at all in pursuit.
sentences.zh: 所以追击的人数一点也不多。

sentences.en: And he turns up, uh, in Alexandria and he is presented with Pompey's head on a kind of silver salver and Caesar, Caesar affects the weep.
sentences.zh: 他出现在，呃，亚历山大，有人把庞培的头颅放在一个银盘上呈献给他，而凯撒，凯撒假装痛哭流涕。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe he did.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许他真的哭了。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: So here's the fascinating thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，最迷人的地方就在这里。

sentences.en: So Caesar has come in pursuit of Pompey.
sentences.zh: 凯撒是为了追击庞培而来的。

sentences.en: He gets to Alexandria, you know, this, this sort of strange semi-colony, I guess, or semi-detached
sentences.zh: 他到达了亚历山大，你知道的，这是一个奇怪的半殖民地，我想，或者说处于罗马帝国边缘的半独立……

sentences.en: colony or whatever you want to call it on the fringe of the Roman sort of the Roman imperium.
sentences.zh: 殖民地，或者随你管它叫什么，反正是在罗马帝国权力的边缘。

sentences.en: But you know, the greatest city in the world, I mean, it's larger at this point than Rome.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，这是世界上最伟大的城市，我的意思是，此时它比罗马还要宏大。

sentences.en: The richest city, exactly.
sentences.zh: 最富有的城市，没错。

sentences.en: The richest city in the world.
sentences.zh: 世界上最富有的城市。

sentences.en: So Caesar arrives, it's the first time he's been to Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 所以凯撒到了，这是他第一次来到亚历山大。

sentences.en: Um, this Greek city, he gets off his boat, all these people are there.
sentences.zh: 呃，这座希腊城市，他下了船，所有这些人都在那儿。

sentences.en: They say, here's the head of your enemy.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这是你敌人的头颅。

sentences.en: We've cut it off for you.
sentences.zh: 我们为你把它砍下来了。

sentences.en: And yeah, famously, Tom, he starts crying and says, Oh, what a terrible shame Pompey was a
sentences.zh: 而且，正如大伙所知，汤姆，他开始哭泣并说道：“噢，太遗憾了，庞培是个……”

sentences.en: Roman.
sentences.zh: “罗马人。”

sentences.en: But he's obviously secretly incredibly relieved.
sentences.zh: 但他显然暗地里松了一大口气。

sentences.en: Do you think, or do you, so how seriously does Caesar take this business, this ideological business of he's a Roman, how dare you cut his head off?
sentences.zh: 你觉得，或者说，凯撒对这种意识形态——即“他是罗马人，你们怎么敢砍他的头”——到底有多认真？

sentences.en: I think that he feels genuine grief because the men had been close.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他感到了真正的悲伤，因为这两人曾关系密切。

sentences.en: I think that as a Roman, he thinks it's outrageous that as great a figure as Pompey has been dispatched by people you may well describe as fleshy and oily.
sentences.zh: 我认为作为一名罗马人，他觉得像庞培这样伟大的人物竟然被你们这些可以说是又胖又油腻的人干掉，简直是奇耻大辱。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, because those are absolutely the terms in which Romans regard sinister kind of Hellenistic Greeks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，因为这绝对是罗马人看待阴险的希腊化希腊人的常用词汇。

sentences.en: Tom, I think beheading people on boats is poor form.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得在船上砍人脑袋这种做法太没风度了。

sentences.en: I'm not going to apologise for, dissing Theodotus.
sentences.zh: 对于贬低狄奥多图斯这件事，我是绝不会道歉的。

sentences.en: You know, the shrewdest political player, one of the shrewdest who's ever lived.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是最精明的政治玩家之一，是有史以来最精明的人之一。

sentences.en: Of course, he understands that this is a godsend because Pompey has been removed, you know, cleared from the chessboard and he's not responsible.
sentences.zh: 当然，他明白这是天赐良机，因为庞培已经被移除了，你知道的，从棋盘上清理出去了，而且这与他无关。

sentences.en: Well, Tom, here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，关键在于。

sentences.en: You talk about Caesar's shrewdness.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了凯撒的精明。

sentences.en: So Julius Caesar, we talked about him in the Rubicon podcasts.
sentences.zh: 所以尤利乌斯·凯撒，我们在卢比孔河播客中讨论过他。

sentences.en: He's this incredibly experienced, shrewd, cunning, ruthless commander.
sentences.zh: 他是一位经验极其丰富、精明、狡猾且冷酷无情的统帅。

sentences.en: And now he does something quite odd.
sentences.zh: 而现在他做了一件相当奇怪的事。

sentences.en: So he takes his small forces, you said, and he basically says, let's go to the palace quarter.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他带着他的少量军队，基本上说：我们去王宫区吧。

sentences.en: Let's occupy the palace quarter and establish ourselves there.
sentences.zh: 让我们占领王宫区并在那里建立据点。

sentences.en: Even though the Alexandrian crowd are absolutely furious to see him.
sentences.zh: 尽管亚历山大的民众看到他时愤怒至极。

sentences.en: And clearly the mood of the city is very much against him.
sentences.zh: 而且显然整个城市的情绪都非常排斥他。

sentences.en: And he sort of barricades himself into this sort of compound.
sentences.zh: 他把自己像这样 barricade（筑垒）在这个复合建筑里。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, not only that, but he behaves absolutely as a kind of plenipotentiary.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他的行为完全就像一个全权代表。

sentences.en: He summons both
sentences.zh: 他召集了……

sentences.en: Ptolemy XIII and Cleopatra into his presence.
sentences.zh: 托勒密十三世和克利奥帕特拉来到他面前。

sentences.en: And he is going to decide which of them should rule and what the ordering of Egypt should be.
sentences.zh: 他要决定他们俩谁该统治，以及埃及的秩序该如何建立。

sentences.en: And I think the reason that he does this, well, he needs the money.
sentences.zh: 我想他这么做的原因，好吧，他需要钱。

sentences.en: He also has a civil war.
sentences.zh: 他还有一场内战要打。

sentences.en: He has a civil war to continue fighting.
sentences.zh: 他还有内战要继续打下去。

sentences.en: You know, he's defeated
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他击败了……
